title: COVID-19 lockdown effect on retail foot traffic

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with Event Study Extension**

This is a classic DID setting: we have a clear treatment group (stores in strict lockdown counties) and control group (stores in minimal restriction counties), with a well-defined treatment timing (March 2020, period 4). The panel structure with pre- and post-periods is ideal for DID.

**Key Assumptions:**
1. **Parallel Trends:** Absent the lockdown orders, foot traffic in strict-lockdown and minimal-restriction counties would have followed parallel trends. We test this with an event study checking that pre-treatment period-by-treatment interactions are jointly zero.
2. **No Anticipation:** Stores did not significantly alter behavior before the official lockdown orders.
3. **No Spillovers (SUTVA):** Foot traffic in control counties was not affected by lockdowns in treated counties.
4. **Stable Composition:** No differential store closures/openings across groups during the sample period.

## 2. R Code

```r
# =============================================================================
# COVID-19 Lockdown Effect on Retail Foot Traffic: DID Analysis
# =============================================================================

library(fixest)
library(data.table)

# --- Load Data ---
df <- fread("experiments/exp_b/data/s01_data.csv")
cat("=== Data Overview ===\n")
cat("Dimensions:", nrow(df), "rows x", ncol(df), "cols\n")
cat("Stores:", length(unique(df$unit_id)), "\n")
cat("Periods:", sort(unique(df$period)), "\n")
cat("Treated stores:", sum(df$treated[df$period == 1]), "\n")
cat("Control stores:", sum(df$treated[df$period == 1] == 0), "\n\n")

# Summary statistics by group and time
cat("=== Mean Foot Traffic by Group and Period ===\n")
summary_tab <- df[, .(mean_y = mean(y), sd_y = sd(y), n = .N), 
                   by = .(treated, post)]
print(summary_tab)
cat("\n")

# More detailed: by period
period_means <- df[, .(mean_y = mean(y)), by = .(treated, period)]
period_means <- dcast(period_means, period ~ treated, value.var = "mean_y")
setnames(period_means, c("0", "1"), c("Control", "Treated"))
period_means[, Diff := Treated - Control]
cat("=== Period-Level Means ===\n")
print(period_means)
cat("\n")

# =============================================================================
# MODEL 1: Basic DID (pooled OLS with interaction)
# =============================================================================
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("MODEL 1: Basic Two-Way DID\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
m1 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post + treated + post, data = df)
summary(m1)
cat("\n")

# =============================================================================
# MODEL 2: TWFE DID with Store and Period Fixed Effects
# =============================================================================
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("MODEL 2: TWFE DID (Store + Period FE)\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
m2 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df)
summary(m2)
cat("\nDID Estimate (TWFE):", round(coef(m2)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("SE:", round(se(m2)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("t-stat:", round(coef(m2)["treat_x_post"] / se(m2)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n\n")

# =============================================================================
# MODEL 3: TWFE with Clustered Standard Errors at Store Level
# =============================================================================
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("MODEL 3: TWFE DID with Clustered SE (store level)\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
m3 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
            cluster = ~unit_id, data = df)
summary(m3)
cat("\n")

# =============================================================================
# MODEL 4: Event Study (Dynamic DID) — Parallel Trends Test
# =============================================================================
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("MODEL 4: Event Study / Dynamic DID\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

# Create relative time variable (treatment at period 4)
df[, rel_time := period - 4]

# Use period 3 (rel_time = -1) as reference
df[, rel_time_factor := factor(rel_time)]

# Event study with store and period FE
m4 <- feols(y ~ i(rel_time, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period, 
            cluster = ~unit_id, data = df)
summary(m4)

cat("\n=== Event Study Coefficients ===\n")
es_coefs <- coef(m4)
es_se <- se(m4)
for (i in seq_along(es_coefs)) {
  cat(sprintf("  %s: %7.4f (SE: %.4f, p: %.4f)\n", 
              names(es_coefs)[i], es_coefs[i], es_se[i],
              2 * pt(-abs(es_coefs[i]/es_se[i]), df = 198)))
}

# --- Pre-trend test: joint significance of pre-treatment coefficients ---
cat("\n=== Pre-Trends Test ===\n")
pre_coefs <- grep("rel_time::-[2-3]", names(coef(m4)), value = TRUE)
if (length(pre_coefs) > 0) {
  pre_test <- wald(m4, keep = pre_coefs)
  print(pre_test)
} else {
  cat("Pre-period coefficients: checking manually\n")
  pre_indices <- grep("::-", names(coef(m4)))
  if (length(pre_indices) > 0) {
    pre_vals <- coef(m4)[pre_indices]
    pre_ses <- se(m4)[pre_indices]
    cat("Pre-treatment coefficients:\n")
    for (j in seq_along(pre_vals)) {
      cat(sprintf("  %s = %.4f (SE=%.4f)\n", names(pre_vals)[j], pre_vals[j], pre_ses[j]))
    }
  }
}

# =============================================================================
# ROBUSTNESS CHECKS
# =============================================================================
cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("ROBUSTNESS CHECKS\n")
cat("============================================================\n")

# Robustness 1: County-level clustering (if treated proxies county)
cat("\n--- Robustness 1: Clustering at treatment-group level ---\n")
m_rob1 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
                cluster = ~treated, data = df)
cat("DID coef:", round(coef(m_rob1)["treat_x_post"], 4),
    " SE:", round(se(m_rob1)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")

# Robustness 2: No fixed effects (simple DID)
cat("\n--- Robustness 2: Simple DID (no FE) ---\n")
m_rob2 <- feols(y ~ treated * post, data = df)
cat("DID coef:", round(coef(m_rob2)["treated:post"], 4),
    " SE:", round(se(m_rob2)["treated:post"], 4),
    " p-value:", round(pvalue(m_rob2)["treated:post"], 6), "\n")

# Robustness 3: Restrict to balanced panel check
cat("\n--- Robustness 3: Balanced panel check ---\n")
obs_per_store <- df[, .N, by = unit_id]
cat("Min obs per store:", min(obs_per_store$N), "\n")
cat("Max obs per store:", max(obs_per_store$N), "\n")
cat("All stores have 8 periods:", all(obs_per_store$N == 8), "\n")

# Robustness 4: Placebo test — fake treatment at period 2
cat("\n--- Robustness 4: Placebo Test (fake treatment at period 2) ---\n")
df_pre <- df[period <= 3]  # Only pre-treatment periods
df_pre[, fake_post := as.integer(period >= 2)]
df_pre[, fake_treat_post := treated * fake_post]
m_placebo <- feols(y ~ fake_treat_post | unit_id + period, 
                   cluster = ~unit_id, data = df_pre)
cat("Placebo DID coef:", round(coef(m_placebo)["fake_treat_post"], 4),
    " SE:", round(se(m_placebo)["fake_treat_post"], 4),
    " p-value:", round(pvalue(m_placebo)["fake_treat_post"], 4), "\n")

# Robustness 5: Separate post-period effects
cat("\n--- Robustness 5: Post-Period Heterogeneity ---\n")
df[, post_period := ifelse(post == 0, "pre", paste0("post_", period - 3))]
df[, post_period := factor(post_period)]
m_hetero <- feols(y ~ i(post_period, treated, ref = "pre") | unit_id + period,
                  cluster = ~unit_id, data = df)
summary(m_hetero)

# =============================================================================
# SUMMARY TABLE
# =============================================================================
cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("SUMMARY: Model Comparison\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
etable(m1, m3, m4, 
       headers = c("Basic DID", "TWFE Clustered", "Event Study"),
       se.below = TRUE)

# =============================================================================
# FINAL RESULT
# =============================================================================
cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("MAIN RESULT\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
main_coef <- round(coef(m3)["treat_x_post"], 4)
main_se <- round(se(m3)["treat_x_post"], 4)
main_ci_lo <- round(main_coef - 1.96 * main_se, 4)
main_ci_hi <- round(main_coef + 1.96 * main_se, 4)
main_pval <- round(pvalue(m3)["treat_x_post"], 6)

cat(sprintf("ATT (DID estimate): %.4f\n", main_coef))
cat(sprintf("Clustered SE: %.4f\n", main_se))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", main_ci_lo, main_ci_hi))
cat(sprintf("p-value: %.6f\n", main_pval))
cat(sprintf("\nInterpretation: Strict lockdowns %s foot traffic by approximately %.1f%%\n",
            ifelse(main_coef < 0, "reduced", "increased"),
            abs((exp(main_coef) - 1) * 100)))
cat("(since y is in log units, exp(coef)-1 gives approximate % change)\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Sign:** The DID coefficient (`treat_x_post`) should be **negative and statistically significant**. Stores in counties with strict lockdown orders should experience larger declines in foot traffic compared to stores in counties with minimal restrictions.

**Magnitude:** Given the severity of COVID-19 lockdowns in March–May 2020, I expect:
- A DID estimate in the range of **-1.0 to -3.0 log points** (corresponding to roughly 60–95% decline in relative foot traffic). Given this is simulated data, the effect could be more moderate, perhaps around **-1.5 to -2.5 log points**.
- The effect may be heterogeneous across post-periods: the largest decline likely in periods 4–5 (March–April 2020), with partial recovery in periods 6–7 (May onward), which the event study will reveal.

**Pre-trends:** The event study pre-treatment coefficients should be statistically insignificant and close to zero, validating the parallel trends assumption — foot traffic trends were similar across treated and control counties before the lockdown.

**Robustness:** The placebo test (fake treatment in the pre-period) should yield a null result, confirming no differential pre-trends. Results should be stable across clustering choices and model specifications.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=strict-lockdown counties, control=minimal-restriction counties; shock=March 2020 lockdown
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Strict-lockdown stores show significantly lower foot traffic post-lockdown
_ground_truth.main_effect: ~30% decline in foot traffic for treated stores
